elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Grant runs "for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations" — affiliate coverage is pre-existing and retained unchanged (subject only to the same Authorized Locations/additional-fee limit that applies to Sparkling itself).

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Rendered grant names only Sparkling and its affiliated companies; no words extending use to contractors or third parties acting on Sparkling's behalf were inserted, and Section 3(c) still bars sublicensing of the Work absent Garman's written authorization.

The rendered grant contains no term language (no "perpetual", no stated duration); the drafter asserts perpetuity-while-fees-are-paid but no operative text evidencing an unconditional paid-up perpetual term is before us.

No "irrevocable" wording appears in the rendered grant; the absence of an express at-will revocation right (regex "no at-will revocation remains") is not the same as an affirmative irrevocability covenant.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The cited text describes a licence with a Fee Schedule for extra locations but no subscription structure or licence-termination trigger is in evidence, so the condition for this element cannot be resolved on the operative language supplied.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Sparkling may transfer this licence to a successor by merger or acquisition without Garman's approval." Narrower than "successors" generally (e.g. an asset-sale successor is not expressly covered), but a successor transfer right now exists in the grant.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are covered automatically in the grant ("affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations") with no notice condition, which meets and exceeds the fallback minimum; no edit was needed or made.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: New grant sentence gives a direct, unconditional transfer right to "a successor by merger or acquisition without Garman's approval"; the conflicting "non-transferable" modifier was deleted and Section 3(c) was conformed ("except as permitted by Section 2 or as and when authorized...").

reasons: Fallback level is complete: affiliate coverage was already unconditional in the grant, and the inserted sentence supplies an express M&A successor transfer right exercisable without Garman's approval.

Preferred level is not complete: no contractor extension, no express "irrevocable" wording, and no perpetual-term language for a paid-up licence in the operative text; the subscription-termination element cannot be resolved from the supplied clauses.

Minimality holds. Three surgical touches — deletion of the contradictory "non-transferable" modifier, one sentence adding the successor right, and a conforming carve-out in Section 3(c) which would otherwise prohibit transferring the Work to any Person. Nothing outside the transferability element was altered; "non-exclusive", the Authorized Locations limit and the additional-fee mechanic all survive, and no survival tail, expense or procedural boilerplate was added.

Intent is preserved: the mutual assignment clause in Section 20(d) was deliberately left untouched, so no new Vendor-side assignment exception was created. The direct "without Garman's approval" permission in the grant is the sanctioned route over a broad notwithstanding override; Section 20(d) is the general clause and the grant sentence the specific permission.

Repair before sending (drafting hygiene, not a checklist failure): confirm that the grant paragraph is in fact Section 2 before relying on the cross-reference "except as permitted by Section 2" in Section 3(c) — if the grant sits in another numbered section, the carve-out becomes a dangling reference and the Section 3(c) prohibition would revive against the successor transfer. Consider "except as permitted by the licence grant in Section [X]" once verified.

If you want to reach the preferred level in a later round, the specific additions required are: (i) "and contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf" in the grant's beneficiary list, (ii) an express "perpetual and irrevocable upon payment of the licence fees" term, and (iii) if any part of the licence is subscription-based, a statement that it may be terminated only for material breach that remains uncured after notice.
